def merge_intervals(intervals):
    if not intervals:
        return []
    intervals = sorted(intervals, key=lambda x: x[0])
    merged = [intervals[0]]
    for start, end in intervals[1:]:

        if start <= last_end:
            merged[-1] = [last_start, max(last_end, end)]
        else:
            merged.append([start, end])
    return merged

Let the original price be $P$.

After a 20% discount you pay

$P_{1}=P\,(1-0.20)=0.80\,P$

i.e. 80% of the original.

A 25% rise on that discounted price is

$P_{2}=P_{1}\,(1+0.25)=0.80P\times1.25$

$P_{2}=P\times0.80\times1.25=P\times1.00$

The 25% increase is 25% of the *reduced* amount, not 25% of the
original.  $0.25\times0.80P =0.20P$, so the 20% you took off is put back
on:

$0.80P+0.25\times0.80P =0.80P+0.20P =P$.

In this particular numbers the two moves cancel.  In general a
percent-off followed by a percent-on is not symmetric because the
second percent is taken on a different base.
